title: A type-state connection
description:
Make wrong orders of calls impossible to compile.

```
connect -> authenticate("secret") -> send("hello")   ok
send before authenticate                              does not compile
wrong password                                        Err("wrong password"), back to Connected
```
hints: Each state change consumes `self` and builds a `Connection` of the new type with the same log (lesson 7.05).
Methods in `impl Connection<Authenticated> { ... }` exist only for that state, so `send` on a `Connection<Connected>` is a compile error.
requirements: `struct Connection<S> { log: Vec<String>, _state: PhantomData<S> }` with states `Disconnected`, `Connected` and `Authenticated` (empty structs).
`connect(self) -> Connection<Connected>`, `authenticate(self, pw) -> Result<Connection<Authenticated>, (Connection<Connected>, String)>`, `send(&mut self, msg)` only on `Authenticated`.
Leave a commented-out line in `main` that would not compile, and say why.
stretch: Add `disconnect(self)` available in every state with one generic `impl<S> Connection<S>`.
